clue.text: Finished with jazz, which is an economic improvement

parts.note: something finished or over is up, as in 'time's up'
swing is a style of big-band jazz

explanation.surface: Done with jazz music, which somehow counts as a boost to the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn in trade or growth is a recovery, the sense of the word in economic reporting.

clue.text: Climbers' support for each different goal

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: different says the letters of goal are made into something else

explanation.surface: Mountaineers' backing for each team that has a different target.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden arbour of posts and beams holds up climbing plants such as roses and vines.

clue.text: Beam, being escorted by welcoming date

indicators.note: welcoming says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: to be escorted by someone is to be with them

explanation.surface: A smiling person escorted by a partner welcomes the date warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's beam is its breadth at the widest point, a measure of how broad it is.

clue.text: In the sack dress?

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, so this is a dress worn in bed

explanation.definitionFit: A loose gown worn in bed is the dress one wears in the sack, slang for bed.

clue.text: Say "proceed", being loveless, answerless intellectual

parts.note: say, meaning for example, is abbreviated eg

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and loveless says that letter is dropped
A stands for answer, and answerless says that letter is removed

parts.note: to proceed is to go ahead

explanation.surface: Someone told to proceed, unloved and without answers, is nonetheless a brainbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being loveless, answerless' asks for two deletions from the phrase for proceed: the zero of love and the A for answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow, bookish person is mockingly called this, an informal noun for a thinker.

clue.text: Sandy, the pop performer with a different intro?

indicators.note: a different intro means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a pop performer is a singer

explanation.surface: A sandy-haired pop star tries a new opening to the song.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer too: Ginger Rogers is the 6 of the puzzle, Fred Astaire's dance partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy and ginger both describe reddish-yellow hair, so they are colour synonyms.

clue.text: He's first — I say! I say! — to secure vote for the common people

indicators.note: the first letter of the word
to secure means to hold fast, so the doubled call holds the vote inside

parts.note: oi is a call for attention, like I say!, so the pair gives it twice
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine opener, I say! I say!, then a secure vote for the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say! I say!' is the old music-hall comedian's patter opener; 'to secure' has the doubled call wrapped around the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek for the many, the phrase is a slightly sneering term for the masses.

clue.text: One with no faith in Panama (the isthmus)

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A nonbeliever in Panama, the narrow land bridge between the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is pan(AMA THE IST)hmus, skipping the bracket and space.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies the existence of God has no religious belief.

clue.text: 10 or 6 humorously: "I echo partner's movement"

indicators.note: movement says the letters move to new places, rearranged

parts.note: taken with its final s as a letter

explanation.surface: A dancer describing how they mirror a partner's steps.
explanation.walkthrough: Terpsichore is the Greek muse of dance, so the word is a jokey label for a dancer like Fred Astaire or Ginger Rogers.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective, from Terpsichore, muse of dance, is a mock-grand word for a dancer.

clue.text: "Motivated? Not I": TV family man from way back

definitions.text: TV family man from way back

indicators.note: 'Not I' asks for the letter I to be left out of the word before

parts.note: someone motivated is fired up, so fired

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off being motivated, like a lazy old sitcom father.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme pairs Fred Astaire with Ginger Rogers, but this clue's definition points to Fred Flintstone, the 1960s cartoon father.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Flintstone is the head of the Stone Age cartoon family, a man from way back in both senses.

clue.text: Raw, easy to digest is OK

parts.note: raw, as in inexperienced or unripe, means green
a light meal is one easy to digest

explanation.surface: Uncooked food that sits lightly on the stomach gets approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a project the go-ahead is to approve it, so the phrase works as a verb for sanction.

clue.text: Work in which in which 10 and 6 appeared

definitions.text: Work in which in which 10 and 6 appeared

parts.words: Work in which in which 10 and 6 appeared
parts.note: the work is the 1935 musical film starring Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, named after formal headwear

explanation.definitionFit: The 1935 film starring Astaire and Rogers is titled after a gentleman's tall silk hat.

clue.text: Airport complex round back of Dodge City

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the piece that follows
complex here means intricately mixed up, signalling the letters of airport are rearranged
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An airport building surrounds the rear of Dodge City in the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge City' wants to be read together as the Kansas town, but 'Dodge' gives only its last letter E, and 'City' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital, a city.

clue.text: Sort of meal had by lovers when the electricity's lacking?

definitions.text: Sort of meal had by lovers
definitions.meaning: a romantic dinner lit by wax tapers
in a power cut the only light comes from wax tapers

explanation.definitionFit: A romantic dinner is lit by tapers, as would any meal be in a power cut.

clue.text: See 22
Sudden concentrated effort of baronet intertwined with Ms Taylor?

indicators.note: intertwined says the two pieces are woven together, their letters mixed

parts.note: Liz Taylor, the film star Elizabeth Taylor

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman entangled with Elizabeth Taylor makes a sudden all-out campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intertwined with' mixes the title's abbreviation in among the letters of the actress's pet name rather than setting them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is an intense burst of activity, from the German for lightning attack.

clue.text: Give birth, warranting opening of Spanish hock

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine merchant must start production, warranting a new vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and frogs produce young by laying eggs in numbers, a verb for producing offspring.

clue.text: Appropriate type of stitch with ring in

parts.note: purl is a knitting stitch
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Use the right kind of stitch with a ring sewn in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable but is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without permission, a synonym for steal.

clue.text: Casual T-shirt, the one for Sally's first milestone birthday?

indicators.note: casual, as in loose or haphazard, signals the letters are rearranged
one for a letter means it takes that letter's place
the first letter of the name

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A casual T-shirt, the right one to give Sally on her big birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for Sally's first' swaps the S of T-SHIRT for I, giving TIHIRT; 'Casual' rearranges that with THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning thirty is a landmark age, and the day itself is the thirtieth birthday.

clue.text: Full up but said "Tuck again!"

indicators.note: said shows the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: to tuck fabric is to fold it, so to tuck again is to re-pleat

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed full is still told to tuck in again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck' looks like food (British slang for snacks) or tucking in to eat, but here it is a fold sewn into cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially after a big meal.

clue.text: Half of 10 and 6's supporters certainly not describing what either 10 or 6 had

definitions.meaning: the two dancers stand on four ... between them, and half of those, two, are their left ones

definitions.text: certainly not describing what either 10 or 6 had
definitions.meaning: the idiom for a clumsy dancer, the opposite of Astaire and Rogers

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hopeless at dancing; literally two of the pair's four feet are left ones.

clue.text: Wrong foot idly in — disastrous for 10 and 6's first screen pairing

indicators.note: disastrous suggests the words are wrecked and thrown together in a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy misstep that would be disastrous for a famous dancing duo's first film together.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1933 film starring Dolores del Río was the first to pair Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1933 musical was the first film to put Astaire and Rogers together on screen.

clue.text: One who goes on applying pressure to snake

indicators.note: applying, as in putting one thing onto another, sets the first piece against the front of the second

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a rattler is a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps pressing a snake for a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer talks on and on, so one who goes on is a babbler.

clue.text: Shakespearean character used in an infamous theatrical assassination

definitions.meaning: Ensign ... is a swaggering soldier in Henry IV Part 2, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

definitions.text: used in an infamous theatrical assassination
definitions.meaning: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln with a derringer handgun at Ford's Theatre in 1865

explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln was killed with a small handgun in a theatre, and Falstaff's swaggering crony bears that name.

clue.text: Chesterfield, possibly on far left side of road up to this point

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a chesterfield is a type of buttoned leather sofa

indicators.note: the far left side of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Chesterfield sofa dumped on the far left side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means until now, as in so far so good.

clue.text: Organise indoor activity (being squeezed by Ms Blanchett)

indicators.note: being squeezed by puts the rearranged letters inside the actress's name

parts.note: Cate Blanchett, the Australian actress

indicators.note: activity suggests the letters of indoor are busy moving, rearranged

explanation.surface: An indoor pastime has someone squashed up against Cate Blanchett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activity' rearranges the indoor letters, and 'being squeezed by' has the actress's first name close around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate a project is to arrange and manage its parts, a synonym for organise.

clue.text: See 21
Attempt to infiltrate Green movement? Get stuffed!

indicators.note: to infiltrate says the first piece goes inside the rearranged letters
movement suggests the letters of green are shifted around

parts.note: an attempt is a go, as in have a go

explanation.surface: Someone tries to infiltrate the environmental movement and is told to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuffed!' looks like a rude retort but is read literally; 'movement' rearranges Green and 'to infiltrate' puts the attempt inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To engorge is to fill to excess, so the rude retort is read literally as a command to fill up.

clue.text: River birds which Piaf apparently didn't have

parts.note: egrets are white herons

explanation.surface: River birds that, oddly, the French singer Piaf claimed not to have.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Piaf's famous song is 'Non, je ne regrette rien': I regret nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Piaf sang that she had no remorse about anything, so these are what she lacked.
